chunks: From him, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Washa, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Yahya ibn Abi al-A'ala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The prayer of Al-Zawal is the prayer of the repentant.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, a title for Imam Ali (peace be upon him).
key_terms.الْأَوَّابِينَ: The repentant; those who frequently return to God in repentance and devotion.
key_terms.صَلَاةُ الزَّوَالِ: The midday prayer, a specific optional prayer performed after the sun passes its zenith.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the midday prayer (Salat al-Zawal) in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this chain linking Imam Ali to the Prophet’s successor, identifying the midday optional prayer (Salat al-Zawal) as the 'prayer of the repentant.' This designation highlights the spiritual discipline of returning to God during the heat of the day, a practice emphasized in Shia jurisprudence for cultivating humility and consistency in worship beyond the obligatory five daily prayers.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa, from Aban Bin Usman, from Yahya Bin Abu Al A’ala, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘The midday Salāt is the Salāt of the repentant’.
en.sarwar: 10. It is a narration from him (narrator of previous Hadith) by Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from Yahya’ ibn abu al-‘Ala’ who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
’Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, “Salah (prayer) at noontime is Salah (prayer) of repenting people.’””
